title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, precise execution accounting, a representative validator-trace excerpt, quantitative analysis, failure-mode diagnostics, and artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps workflows with generative models requires reliable mechanisms to avoid harmful, silent, or wrong-but-plausible actions. A common operational pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a generator (LLM) proposes a candidate configuration or plan, a deterministic validator mechanically checks correctness and policy constraints, and, when necessary, a repair module synthesizes corrected candidates or triggers human review. Prior demonstrations of GVR-like architectures in code and system domains motivate their adoption in NetOps, but systematic, preregistered measurements of validator coverage (false-positive/false-negative rates), detection latency, and predictive usefulness for end-to-end guarded success are scarce [1].

We preregistered study AC-2026-03 with a paired design that isolates the effect of downstream validator-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task the generator produced a single initial candidate that was reused by both the baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator+repair permitted) conditions. Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise downstream from validator-triggered repair, not from independent generator sampling. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (H1) expected that a multidimensional validator-metric suite would explain more variance in end-to-end success than a single verifier pass rate. Our main contribution here is a fully preregistered, artifact-archived experiment and an exact, transparent report of a degenerate confirmatory outcome (ceiling) with concrete, artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up designs that can measure validator utility.
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair and closed-loop verifier architectures have been proposed and evaluated in code and system domains to reduce stochastic generator error and to enable deterministic acceptance criteria; these works provide the architectural motivation for inserting mechanical validators into NetOps GVR flows [1]. Recent NetOps and AIOps benchmark efforts document substantive failure modes—ticket noise, false premises, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that complicate end-to-end automation and motivate insertion of verifier layers; these benchmarks emphasize controlled evaluation of agentic behaviours rather than production deployment outcomes [2],[3]. Prototype system reports propose self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair to reduce silent or action-triggering failures in tool-augmented LLM systems; these reports show feasibility but do not deliver standardized validator-metric suites for NetOps [4]. Broader surveys of LLMs for telecommunications and NetOps discuss adaptation and verification trade-offs and motivate metricized evaluation of verification cost versus nominal correctness [5].

Synthesizing these records: the existing literature supports the proposition that verifier layers can mechanistically detect many structural or syntactic faults and that verifier-guided corrections improve outcomes in controlled demonstrations. However, a persistent gap remains: quantitative, preregistered protocols and public artifact bundles to estimate validator FP/FN, coverage, and operational-impact prediction for NetOps GVR flows. Our study was designed to start closing this gap under strict preregistration and archived-execution practices; we treat prior demonstrations as architectural and motivational rather than as establishing empirical coverage for NetOps validators.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and study design. The experiment was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Key preregistered elements (excerpted from the frozen manifest): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini; task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false. The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the primary test was an exact two-sided McNemar with paired bootstrap percentile CIs (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). The preregistration included power planning targeted to detect a 0.10 paired improvement with α = 0.05 and ≈80% power under reasonable baseline scenarios; bootstrap stability checks were preregistered.

Task generation and constraints. Tasks were drawn deterministically from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family intent_configuration_repair_v1) at difficulty levels labelled 'very_hard' and 'extreme'. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, compact intent, allowed_fields, allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence. These structured constraints permit mechanistic validation: the validator checks parsed_command_count versus required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count versus allowed_touched_fields, and policy invariants (protected interfaces, group minima). Task selection followed a deterministic index rule (challenging_workflow_stress_v1) and contamination/exclusion rules (exact-duplicate SHA-256 exclusion; semantic-similarity exclusion when embedding cosine > 0.95). The execution bundle records task_manifest.jsonl and representative task entries; no contamination exclusions occurred in this run (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Model, sampling, and provider audit. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini; execution accounting shows model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair) and maximum_model_calls = 400 as preregistered. Crucially, execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; provider-side sampling may still produce stochastic variability. Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation/provider_call_audit) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with exactly one shared initial generation per task as preregistered.

Validator, scoring, and exclusions. The validator used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The scoring rule for the primary confirmatory estimand was full_intent_constraint_validation: an episode is scored as success when validator.valid == true. The validator emits mechanistic fields per episode (normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, violation_count, repair_applied) and records repair prompts/traces when repairs are requested. The pipeline permitted at most one repair call for rejected candidates; repairs would be recorded and repair_applied = true. The preregistered missingness and exclusion rules were enforced: maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries), and complete-pair analysis was used for the primary test; sensitivity analyses were preregistered to treat missing guarded episodes as failures where appropriate.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (shared-initial generation per pair). No contamination exclusions or near-duplicate replacements occurred. Analysis artifacts: analysis/condition_summary.csv reports baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. These numeric results are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and reproduced verbatim in the execution bundle.

Representative validator-trace exemplar. To illustrate validator semantics and why no repairs were triggered we include an artifact-grounded excerpt from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json (representative pair; values taken verbatim from the archived JSON):
  - pair_id: pair-000004
  - normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
  - parsed_command_count: 4
  - required_command_count: 4
  - observed_touched_field_count: 3
  - valid: true
  - repair_applied: false
  - validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
  - validator_version: 5.0
For this exemplar the parsed/required command counts match, no violation codes were emitted, and the validator did not request repair. Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode; the repair_applied field is false in all 400 episode artifacts.

Diagnostic analyses. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline and guarded conditions evaluated the identical initial candidate per pair; therefore any paired difference could only arise via validator-triggered repair. The degenerate all-valid outcome results from three artifact-observed determinants: (1) the synthetic generator produced candidates satisfying the validator's mechanistic constraints for the recorded generation seeds and generator behaviour; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling regime (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1) removed generator-variability as a source of disagreements between conditions; (3) the deterministic validator enforces syntactic/structural intent-constraints but cannot detect all forms of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure yet incorrect-by-intent). Consequently, no repairs were applied and the confirmatory test could not detect the preregistered 10-percentage-point improvement target.

Secondary and sensitivity notes. Per-validator FP/FN estimates are degenerate (no observed false positives or false negatives). Detection-latency and repair-invocation distributions are uninformative because repair_applied = false for all episodes. The execution bundle nevertheless contains full per-episode validator traces and raw responses (execution/raw_results.jsonl) to support reanalysis under alternative scoring rules or under preregistered injected-fault arms.
sections.discussion:
Inferential consequences. The preregistered paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics is well suited to isolate validator-triggered repair effects, but it concentrates the risk of a single-sample ceiling when the generator and validator align. With baseline success = 1.0 the paired estimator has zero variance; the McNemar test and bootstrap CI are degenerate and uninformative for the originally targeted paired improvement. This outcome is a valid, artifact-reproducible experimental result that indicates the preregistered design—as executed—did not produce data that could test H1 as formulated.

Operational interpretation of validator scope. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) provides reliable mechanistic intent-constraint checks recorded as parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and valid flags. Artifact-grounded evidence here shows that validator.valid == true does not guarantee semantic intent alignment with operator expectations; mechanistic validators are inherently scoped to structural and policy invariants expressible to them. Therefore, absence of detected violations in this synthetic bank should not be interpreted as universal semantic correctness across production scenarios.

Artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments. Using only mechanisms and configuration options already present in the archived adapter and task generator, we record three preregistered follow-up arms that would create estimable baseline failure prevalence and permit measurement of validator FP/FN and repair utility: (A) Fault-injection arm: deterministically inject controlled faults into reference answers for a fraction f of tasks (syntactic errors, configuration-logic faults, semantic-intent swaps). (B) Multi-sample generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task to expose generator variability and permit guarded acceptance among multiple draws. (C) Multi-validator and multi-model comparison: add an alternative validator implementation and an additional model family to quantify sensitivity to validator design and model sampling. Each prescription is implementable with the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter and deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 manifest entries already archived; implementing them would produce non-degenerate, analyzable data appropriate for the originally planned primary and secondary estimands.

Threats to validity and reproducibility. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolates repair effects but introduced single-sample ceiling risk. Construct validity: binary validator.valid operationalizes mechanistic correctness but may fail to capture semantic intent misalignment. External validity: synthetic task bank, single-model (gpt-5-mini), and single deterministic validator limit generalization beyond these controlled conditions. Conclusion validity: the degenerate outcome produced zero variance, preventing inference about validator benefit in this run. All of these limitations are recorded in the execution and analysis artifacts and motivate the artifact-grounded follow-up arms above.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, the sampled gpt-5-mini seeds, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. This result is artifact-grounded and reproducible from the archived bundle. We publish the exact execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and provide concrete, preregistered experiment prescriptions (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) that are required to produce estimable validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions. The artifacts and analysis logs are archived in the execution bundle for community reanalysis and for use as the basis of follow-up preregistered experiments that can resolve the open measurement questions identified here.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
